subtopics: Documented cases of contradictory health and nutrition findings: coffee and health, eggs and cholesterol, alcohol (J-curve debate), dietary fat, hormone replacement therapy (WHI reversal) — and how media coverage amplified or handled the reversals
How professional fact-checkers (IFCN, Snopes, PolitiFact) and information-literacy frameworks (SIFT, lateral reading, CRAAP test) evaluate sources that contain contradictory or ambiguous statements
The distinction between ambiguity, vagueness, and contradiction in legal and analytical writing, and standard phrasing used to declare a source ambiguous or internally inconsistent
